subject: business-studies
title: Business Basics & Startup Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the building blocks of business — aims, sectors and the legal forms a startup can take.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies foundations — business aims, the three sectors and legal structures explained.
final_note: You learned why businesses exist, the three sectors of the economy, and the main legal structures owners can choose.

concepts.def: A long-term goal a business wants to achieve
Provides services to consumers and businesses
Two or more owners sharing profits and risk

walkthroughs.body_html:
Every business has aims — long-term goals it tries to achieve.

Common aims include making a profit, surviving, growing, helping a social cause, and being independent.

The economy is split into three sectors.

Primary extracts raw materials (a farm). Secondary turns them into goods (a bakery). Tertiary provides services (a hairdresser).

A sole trader is the simplest form — one person, full control, but full unlimited liability if it fails.

A partnership shares the load between 2+ owners but disputes can happen and liability is still unlimited.

mcqs.q: Which sector does a coal mine belong to?
What does 'unlimited liability' mean for a sole trader?
options: Personal assets can be taken to pay business debts

numericals.q: A partnership has 3 partners sharing profits equally. Total profit is £45,000. How much does each receive, in £?
numericals.hint: Divide total profit by number of partners.

free_texts.q: What sector includes services like banking and tourism? One word.
